messages:
Jin T: Starting bring-up for lattice-embed-mini on our standard holdouts. Goal: confirm int6 per-channel + symmetric clipping doesn't regress recall@1 by >2% on product slices.
Priya S: Which slices? short, multi-sentence, customer-snippets?
Jin T: short_queries, multi_sentence_paraphrase, customer_support_redacted (30 queries), and kmeans-cluster-sample (40k).
Nico R: Please test cosine and L2, we've seen L2 help with small-dim models. Also run id-flip k=1.
Jin T: running harness now. Command:
```
python -m eval.run --model lattice-embed-mini --quant per-channel-int6 --clipping symmetric 6.0 --slices short_queries,multi_sentence_paraphrase,customer_support_redacted,kmeans-cluster-sample --metrics recall@1,recall@5,silhouette,id_flip --sim_metric cosine,l2 --seeds 3 --pca 192 --whiten true
```
Dana K: Add `--normalize true` pre-quantization; normalize then quant seems to help with dot-product scaling.
Jin T: added normalize. First seed (seed=42) quick results (single-seed):
```
slice                       fp32_recall1  int6_recall1  delta  fp32_sil  int6_sil  idflip
short_queries               0.432         0.424         -0.008  0.11     0.10     0.026
multi_sentence_paraphrase  0.728         0.712         -0.016  0.24     0.22     0.031
customer_support_redacted   0.564         0.553         -0.011  0.15     0.14     0.018
kmeans-cluster-sample      0.694         0.681         -0.013  0.20     0.18     0.029
```
Priya S: Deltas look within tolerance for int6. id-flip ~2-3% across slices. Good. How about int4?
Jin T: I ran int4 per-tensor as a quick check: short_queries recall1 dropped to 0.362 (delta -0.07). Not acceptable.
Nico R: For int6, can you produce nearest-neighbor score histogram differences? I want to see if scores compress near top.
Jin T: Sure. fp32 vs int6 top1 score mean: fp32 0.78, int6 0.75; stddev fp32 0.11, int6 0.105. Small compression.
Jin T: Ran 3 seeds, aggregated means (avg over seeds):
```
slice short_queries recall1: fp32 0.430 +/-0.003  int6 0.421 +/-0.004  delta -0.009
slice multi_sentence_paraphrase recall1: fp32 0.726 +/-0.002  int6 0.714 +/-0.003  delta -0.012
customer_support_redacted recall1: fp32 0.561 +/-0.004 int6 0.551 +/-0.003 delta -0.010
```
Dana K: Nice. What's the cluster-level silhouette breakdown? Any clusters collapsing?
Jin T: I computed per-cluster silhouette delta >0.05 only for 2/50 clusters in kmeans sample (those were small clusters <40 points). No major collapse.
Priya S: Perf metrics? memory and latency change?
Jin T: Runtime perf on staging GPU pool: p50 throughput +7%, p99 latency unchanged (within noise). Memory reduced ~24% on exec heap.
Nico R: Recommend canary if ops accepts. Suggest rollout plan: 3% traffic, monitor recall@1 and id-flip per-route, auto-fallback if delta > 2.5% for 5m window.
Jin T: Proposed rollout doc drafted. Will include a small set of customer redacted QA queries to monitor semantic integrity.
ops-bot: Scheduled bench job: bench-3942005678-perf (lattice-embed-mini,int6) queued.
eval-bot: Scheduled eval job started: eval-3942005678-3seeds (lattice-embed-mini, per-channel-int6). ETA ~12m.
Priya S: One more ask: compute recall@1 stratified by query length (1 token, 2-5 tokens, 6+ tokens). We saw short queries are more sensitive.
Jin T: On it — will post stratified table when eval job finishes.
Nico R: Thanks. If stratified shows >3% drop for 1-token queries we may need alternative quant steps (clamping or per-dim rescale).
Dana K: tagging @solutions for impact assessment. :eyes:
